questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Explain what is meant by the following, giving an example of each term: off-the-shelf software, custom-written software. (4 marks)

(b) Give three advantages and one disadvantage of using off-the-shelf software rather than custom written software. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Definitions with examples (4 marks)**

- **Off-the-shelf software** is a ready-made, general-purpose package produced in large numbers for many customers and bought as it is, ready to use at once. Example: Microsoft Word, a spreadsheet package such as Excel, an antivirus program.
- **Custom-written (bespoke) software** is a program designed and written specially to meet the exact requirements of one organisation or user. Example: a patient registration and billing system written for a particular hospital, or a school's examination results system.

**(b) Off-the-shelf against custom-written (4 marks)**

*Three advantages of off-the-shelf software*

1. **Cheaper:** the development cost is shared among many buyers, whereas bespoke software is paid for by one customer.
2. **Available immediately:** it can be bought and installed at once, while custom software takes weeks or months to specify, write and test.
3. **Reliable and well supported:** it has already been used and tested by many users, so most errors have been removed, and documentation, training, updates and user communities are readily available. (Also acceptable: files are easy to exchange with other users of the same package.)

*One disadvantage*

- It is **not designed for the specific needs** of the organisation: it may lack needed features, contain many features that are never used, and be difficult or impossible to modify, so the organisation must adapt its way of working to the software.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An examination centre holds data about candidates at the centre. The data stored for each candidate are:

- 4 digit candidate number.
- Candidate name (30 characters).
- Gender (1 character).
- Date of birth (8 characters).
- Number of subjects registered (2 digit).

(a) If 200 candidates are registered at the centre, calculate the expected size of file to store this information. Show your working and give your answer in bytes. (6 marks)

(b) State a suitable medium for saving a back-up copy of the file in (a) above giving a reason for your answer. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) File size (6 marks)**

Assumption: each character or digit is stored as one ASCII character, that is **1 byte**, and no extra bytes are used for headers or field separators.

| Field | Size (bytes) |
|---|---|
| Candidate number (4 digits) | 4 |
| Candidate name | 30 |
| Gender | 1 |
| Date of birth | 8 |
| Number of subjects (2 digits) | 2 |
| **Size of one record** | $4 + 30 + 1 + 8 + 2 = 45$ |

Size of the file for 200 candidates:

$$200 \times 45 = 9\,000\ \text{bytes}$$

The file is expected to be **9 000 bytes** (about 8.8 KB if 1 KB = 1024 bytes).

**(b) Back-up medium (3 marks)**

A **USB flash drive** (or an external hard disk, or a recordable CD/DVD, or cloud storage) is suitable because:

- its capacity (several gigabytes) is enormously greater than the 9 000 bytes to be saved, so many successive copies fit on it;
- it is small and portable, so the copy can be kept in a **different place** (another building or a safe) and survives a fire, theft or failure of the computer that holds the original file;
- it is cheap, fast to write to and can be reused.
